primitives.name: Neurometabolic cascade of concussion (excitotoxicity vs endogenous neuroprotection)
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is hypothesized that acceleration/deceleration and rotational forces cause diffuse injury to the neurons, which causes an ionic imbalance and release of a cascade of neurotransmitters
primitives.assumptions: Acceleration/deceleration and rotational forces produce diffuse neuronal injury, an ionic imbalance and a neurotransmitter cascade; membrane pumps activate to restore homeostasis producing a brief hyper-metabolic state with lactate accumulation. The outcome of damaged tissue is set by the balance between excitotoxic (glutamatergic, calcium influx, protease/lipase/nuclease activation) and endogenous neuroprotective (GABAergic, cannabinergic) responses. Primary mechanical lesion is irreversible; secondary lesion evolves hours to days.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The cascade is a dynamic, time-evolving process, not a static lesion: symptomology and pathology evolve hourly and over days, so a single acute snapshot misstates severity. The excitotoxicity/neuroprotection balance is photoperiod- and state-dependent (rat TBI recovery differs by time of day; GABA/cannabinoid tone varies circadianly), and forced early exercise is detrimental whereas delayed voluntary sub-threshold exercise is beneficial — the same insult has opposite effects depending on timing and voluntariness.

layer2.mapping: Derived as a two-opposing-processes kernel whose net sign determines tissue fate: an excitatory damage term and an inhibitory protective term compete, and the integrated balance (not either term alone) sets the outcome. In the 22-player football dynamical system this is the structure of a load-vs-recovery kernel after a collision: an acute damage accumulator competes with a recovery/adaptation term, and the net state — modulated by timing (refractory window) and by whether subsequent load is forced or voluntary — determines whether the player adapts or decompensates. The derived discipline is that the sign of the net kernel, and its time-dependence, governs the decision, not the magnitude of the insult alone.
layer2.telemetry: Heart-rate variability (sympathovagal balance), symptom-limited exercise threshold, serial symptom scores, and imaging (DTI fractional anisotropy/mean diffusivity) calibrate the balance; the circadian/state dependence is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from a single acute measurement and requires longitudinal sampling.

primitives.name: Post-Concussion Symptom Scale cutoff false-positive invariant
primitives.verbatim_quote: One study [26] showed this cutoff criterion (7 out of 132) incorrectly labeled 34% of healthy people with PCS, which is higher than people with a concussive head injury (31%).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: s_i = severity rating of the i-th of 22 symptoms on a Likert scale, a dimensionless ordinal integer in {0,...,6} (0 = no symptom, 6 = severe). PCSS = total symptom score, dimensionless integer sum, maximum 22*6 = 132 (dimensionless count). cutoff = 7, a dimensionless score threshold. The reported false-positive rates (34% of healthy labelled, 31% of concussed) are dimensionless probabilities in [0,1]. Healthy-population mean score = 6 (dimensionless). All quantities are dimensionless counts/probabilities; the expression is dimensionally homogeneous.
primitives.assumptions: PCSS is a 22-item self-report Likert checklist (max 132); healthy population averages 6/132; several studies use cutoff 7 to diagnose concussion/PCS. Assumes symptoms are non-specific (occur after other trauma, chronic pain, fatigue, mood disorders), that athletes under-report and secondary-gain subjects over-report, and that no symptom cutoff reliably identifies concussion/PCS.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The cutoff fails catastrophically as a classifier: 7/132 mislabels 34% of healthy people as PCS — a higher false-positive rate than the 31% true-positive rate in concussed patients, i.e. the test is worse than chance at the population level for this threshold. Self-report is biased by effort/secondary gain and can reinforce illness behaviour; there is no gold-standard symptom set diagnostic of PCS or its recovery. The invariant is that a non-specific symptom sum cannot serve as a specific diagnostic gate.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a non-specific aggregate indicator used as a classification gate: summing many loosely-related noisy signals into one score and thresholding it produces a false-positive rate that can exceed the true-positive rate when the signals are not specific to the target state. In the football system this is the error of declaring a player 'injured/unavailable' from a generic wellness/load questionnaire whose items also fire for normal fatigue, mood, or life stress — the gate mislabels healthy players more often than it catches the truly impaired. The source invariant is the specificity failure of a non-specific sum-threshold classifier.
layer2.telemetry: Longitudinal within-player symptom deltas (compare to the player's own baseline rather than a population cutoff), effort/validity indicators, and a specific objective channel (e.g. vestibulo-ocular exam, biomarker panel) calibrate the gate; a single population-thresholded sum is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE for true injury status.

primitives.name: Second Impact Syndrome catastrophic refractory-window threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: SIS occurs when an athlete suffers a concussion and before the first injury has recovered suffers another injury to the head.
primitives.assumptions: SIS occurs when a second head impact is sustained before recovery from a first concussion; the brain has not recovered, so the second injury produces rapid swelling and raised intracranial pressure that, if uncontrolled, can be fatal even after a relatively mild impact. Assumes the existence of a refractory recovery window after the first injury during which autoregulation is impaired, and that cumulative mild head injury (CMHI) causes neural attrition over months/years.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The danger is a nonlinear threshold, not a linear dose-response: a second mild impact inside the unrecovered window can cause catastrophic deterioration and death, disproportionate to the impact magnitude. It is rare but high-consequence and especially significant in young athletes; the risk is governed by the timing relative to the first injury's recovery, not by the second impact's force alone. Outside the refractory window the same impact would not produce SIS.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a refractory-window tail-risk constraint in a cumulative-load system: re-loading a component before it has recovered from a prior shock can trigger a catastrophic, disproportionate failure even when the second load is small. In the 22-player system this is the rule that returning a concussed player to contact before clearance risks a catastrophic second-impact event, and more generally that stacking high-load exposures inside an unrecovered window produces nonlinear tail risk that a linear load model misses. The source invariant is the existence of a recovery-gated catastrophic threshold.
layer2.telemetry: Time-since-first-injury, symptom resolution and clearance status, and graded return-to-play progression calibrate whether the refractory window has closed; the catastrophic threshold itself is a rare-event LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE hazard that must be managed by enforcing the window, not by estimating its probability from frequent data.

primitives.name: Glial/neuronal biomarker ratio (GNR) and complementary-panel classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: The glial/neuronal ratio (GNR) was measured as the quotient between the concentrations of GFAP and UCH-L1.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: [GFAP] = serum concentration of glial fibrillary acidic protein (astrocyte cytoskeleton, blood-brain-barrier disruption marker), mass concentration, SI kg/m^3 expressed clinically in ng/mL. [UCH-L1] = serum concentration of ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase-L1 (neuronal injury marker), same units ng/mL. GNR = ratio of two like-dimensioned concentrations, therefore dimensionless. Reported values: focal lesions ~1.77, diffuse ~0.48, median ~0.85 (all dimensionless); ROC AUC for lesion-type discrimination 0.72 (early <12 h: 0.80), dimensionless probability-scale area. The ratio is dimensionally homogeneous (concentration/concentration).
primitives.assumptions: No single biomarker has both high sensitivity and high specificity; a panel reflecting different mechanisms (glial BBBD vs neuronal injury) and different temporal profiles is required. GNR is independently associated with injury type (focal vs diffuse) but not age/sex/GCS/mechanism; it is more accurate early. ALERT-TBI validated UCH-L1+GFAP within 12 h of mTBI: sensitivity 97.6%, NPV 99.6%, specificity 36.4%, allowing ~1/3 reduction in CT use.
primitives.breakdown_regime: GNR is not an independent predictor of mortality despite being higher in those who died; it discriminates lesion type, not outcome. Single markers fail in polytrauma (extracranial sources elevate S-100β/GFAP, causing false mTBI diagnoses and unnecessary imaging). The panel's high NPV suits rule-out (avoiding CT) but its low specificity (~36%) means a positive result is not confirmatory; extrapolating the mTBI panel to moderate TBI is uncertain.

layer2.mapping: Derived as a complementary-channel classifier: two channels reporting different physical mechanisms (glial barrier disruption vs neuronal injury) with different time constants are fused (here as a ratio) to discriminate a latent injury type that neither channel resolves alone, raising joint AUC above any single channel. In the football system this is the structure of fusing a structural-load channel and a functional-performance channel to classify a player's hidden injury state — the ratio/combination carries information neither observable carries, and the high-NPV/low-specificity asymmetry dictates a rule-out (clear-to-play screening) rather than rule-in use. The derived lesson is to fuse mechanistically distinct channels and to match the decision to the channel's NPV/specificity asymmetry.
layer2.telemetry: Serial serum GFAP and UCH-L1 concentrations with sampling time post-injury, CT/MRI lesion type as the calibration target, and the panel's sensitivity/NPV/specificity calibrate the classifier; without a timed biomarker panel the latent injury type is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from GCS or imaging alone in mild injury.

primitives.name: Brain-tissue hypoxia threshold dominates functional outcome over ICP
primitives.verbatim_quote: brain hypoxia (defined as PbtiO2 < 10 mmHg and for more than 15 minutes) is actually more important in determining the morbidity and patient functional outcome
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P_btiO2 = partial pressure of oxygen in brain tissue, pressure, SI unit pascal (Pa) expressed clinically in mmHg (1 mmHg = 133.322 Pa); threshold 10 mmHg = 1333.22 Pa. Delta t = duration of the low-oxygen state, time, SI unit seconds (s) expressed in minutes (min); threshold 15 min = 900 s. The predicate conjoins a pressure comparison and a time comparison, each unit-consistent, so it is dimensionally homogeneous. ICP (intracranial pressure) and CPP (cerebral perfusion pressure) are also pressures in mmHg; normal supine ICP 7-15 mmHg.
primitives.assumptions: ICP remains the most important determinant of mortality, but brain hypoxia (PbtiO2 < 10 mmHg for > 15 min) is more important for morbidity and functional outcome; ICP/CPP-guided treatment alone does not necessarily prevent hypoxic-ischemic damage. Adding PbtiO2-guided therapy reduces hypoxic-ischemic damage. Mild focal cooling (30-36°C) raised focal brain oxygenation and improved 6-month Glasgow Outcome Score even though ICP/CPP/brain-temperature did not significantly change.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The oxygenation benefit is dissociable from pressure control: in the pilot, decompressive craniectomy had already normalised pressure, so cooling improved oxygenation and outcome without changing ICP/CPP — proving pressure is not the sole causal channel. The Licox probe measures only its local insertion region and cannot reflect whole-brain temperature/oxygenation, so the observable is spatially limited; injured brain can run 0.1 to >2°C above core temperature, and hyperthermia (39-40°C) caused a 2.6-fold increase in hippocampal injury in animals.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a supply-adequacy threshold that dominates outcome over a proxy pressure/throughput metric: a system can show acceptable headline pressure while a local region starves below a critical supply threshold for long enough to cause irreversible damage. In the 22-player system this is the difference between a global load/availability metric looking acceptable while a specific player's local recovery supply (sleep, oxygenation, metabolic clearance) stays below a critical threshold long enough to cause decompensation. The source invariant is that the local supply-duration threshold, not the global proxy, governs functional outcome.
layer2.telemetry: Focal brain tissue oxygen tension (PbtiO2) with dwell time below threshold, ICP/CPP, and brain-vs-core temperature gradient calibrate the hypoxic-insult predicate; a global pressure reading alone is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE for local hypoxia and must be supplemented by a local supply channel.

primitives.name: Flow-metabolism coupling preservation invariant in neuro-sedation
primitives.verbatim_quote: It has to reduce ICP by reducing cerebral blood flow (CBF) or cerebral vasoconstriction, however maintaining the coupling between cerebral blood flow and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen consumption (CMRO2).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: CMRO2 = cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen consumption, volume of O2 per mass of tissue per time, SI mol/(kg·s) expressed clinically as mL O2/(100 g·min). CBF = cerebral blood flow, volume of blood per mass of tissue per time, SI m^3/(kg·s) expressed as mL/(100 g·min). ICP = intracranial pressure, pressure (mmHg; 1 mmHg = 133.322 Pa). CBF/CMRO2 = blood volume delivered per volume of O2 consumed, a dimensionless volume ratio (mL blood / mL O2). CPP = MAP - ICP, a pressure difference in mmHg. The coupling constraint compares like flow quantities and the pressure relation subtracts like pressures, so the expression is dimensionally homogeneous.
primitives.assumptions: The ideal neuro-sedative reduces ICP by reducing CBF/vasoconstriction while maintaining CBF-CMRO2 coupling, preserves cerebral autoregulation and CO2 vascular reactivity, has rapid onset/recovery for wake-up tests, predictable clearance independent of end-organ failure, and minimal hemodynamic depression. Propofol reduces ICP/CMRO2/CBF and preserves coupling/autoregulation but causes dose-dependent hypotension that can lower CPP even while lowering ICP; barbiturates reduce CMRO2 up to 60% during burst suppression with proportional CBF reduction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The coupling invariant is violated by agents or doses that decouple supply from demand: propofol's hypotension can reduce CPP (and thus supply) despite lowering ICP and demand; benzodiazepine/opioid respiratory depression causes hypercapnia that raises ICP; abrupt sedation withdrawal causes cerebral/hemodynamic derangement and energy supply-demand imbalance. Ketamine can increase CMRO2/CBF/ICP. The constraint is therefore a coupling-preservation requirement, not merely 'lower ICP', and fails whenever a pressure or respiratory side-effect breaks the supply-demand match.

layer2.mapping: Derived as a supply-demand coupling constraint on any intervention that throttles a system: lowering demand (CMRO2) is only protective if supply (CBF) is lowered proportionally so the coupling ratio and autoregulation are preserved; an intervention that lowers a headline pressure while breaking the supply-demand match is harmful. In the 22-player system this is the rule that reducing a player's workload is only protective if recovery supply is reduced proportionally and the load-recovery coupling is preserved — cutting training while also cutting sleep/nutrition breaks the coupling and worsens the state despite a lower headline load. The derived discipline is to preserve the coupling ratio, not to optimise a single proxy.
layer2.telemetry: CBF and CMRO2 (or their proxies), ICP/CPP/MAP, EEG burst-suppression ratio, and CO2 reactivity calibrate the coupling; a headline ICP or load number alone is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE for whether supply-demand coupling is preserved and must be paired with a supply-side observable.

reasoning_traces.think: Start from the unifying epistemic problem of this edited volume: the injured brain is a partially observable dynamical system whose true state is repeatedly overwritten by convenient but non-specific proxies. The first invariant, the neurometabolic cascade (p1), establishes that the insult is not a static lesion but a time-evolving competition between an excitotoxic damage process and endogenous GABAergic/cannabinergic protection, with the net balance — not the insult magnitude — setting tissue fate, and with that balance itself modulated by circadian phase and by whether subsequent activity is forced or voluntary. The second invariant, the PCSS cutoff (p2), is the diagnostic shadow of the same problem: a sum of twenty-two non-specific symptoms thresholded at seven mislabels thirty-four percent of healthy people as post-concussional, a higher false-positive rate than the thirty-one percent true-positive rate in the concussed, which means the gate is worse than chance at the population level. Reading p1 and p2 together yields the cognitive source code: a non-specific aggregate cannot stand in for a specific latent state, whether that aggregate is a symptom sum or a single acute snapshot of a dynamic cascade. The retrocausal genealogy is the field's long correction of over-confidence — the explicit statement that 'post-concussion syndrome' is technically not a syndrome because no gold-standard symptom set exists, the recognition that athletes under-report while secondary-gain subjects over-report, and the thirty-year failure of neuroprotective agents translated from animal models (Chapter 5) all descend from the same scar of mistaking a proxy for the mechanism. The theory-of-mind clash is between the clinician's comfort with a tidy numeric gate (a PCSS score, a GCS bucket, a single ICP number) and the patient's actual heterogeneous, evolving state; a clinician who models the patient as a static score will keep applying a classifier that mislabels the healthy and misses the truly impaired. The cross-layer veto fires when the psychometric layer is overruled by the specificity requirement: because the symptom sum is non-specific, the high-EV-looking convenience of a single cutoff is vetoed in favour of longitudinal within-patient deltas plus a mechanistically specific channel (vestibulo-ocular exam, a biomarker panel). The sovereign move is to bind classification to a specific, time-resolved observable and to treat any non-specific sum-threshold as a misleading channel that must be marked unidentifiable when used alone. This is also why the volume insists on comparing each symptom report with the patient's own previous reports rather than a population norm: the within-patient delta restores specificity that the between-population cutoff destroys, and it converts a static, error-prone label into a longitudinal estimate of the evolving cascade's net balance.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The diagnostic humility in this volume was forged by a history of mistaking proxies for mechanisms. The explicit claim that post-concussion syndrome is technically not a syndrome because no gold-standard symptom set diagnoses it or its recovery, the finding that a PCSS cutoff of seven mislabels more healthy people (34%) than it correctly identifies concussed people (31%), and the documented under-reporting by athletes versus over-reporting by secondary-gain subjects all descend from earlier practice that treated a convenient symptom sum as a specific disease gate. Chapter 5's account of thirty years of neuroprotective agents failing to translate from animal models to humans is the same scar at the therapeutic level: the field learned, retrospectively, that a non-specific aggregate or an animal proxy is not the human mechanism, so the modern posture binds classification to specific, longitudinal observables.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Under pressure the clinician's comfort call is a tidy numeric gate — a PCSS total, a GCS bucket, a single acute snapshot — because it resolves the ambiguity of a heterogeneous, evolving patient into one actionable number. The patient's actual state is different: a dynamic neurometabolic cascade whose balance shifts with circadian phase, timing, and whether activity is forced or voluntary, and whose symptoms overlap with normal fatigue, mood, and life stress. A clinician who models the patient as a static score will keep applying a classifier that mislabels the healthy and misses the impaired; correctly modelling the patient as a time-evolving, partially observable system flips the prescription toward within-patient longitudinal deltas and a mechanistically specific confirmatory channel rather than a population cutoff.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The specificity requirement vetoes the high-EV-looking convenience of a single symptom-sum cutoff. The veto fires because the observable the comfort call optimises (a non-specific PCSS total) is not specific to the target state, and the evidence shows its false-positive rate (34% of healthy) exceeds its true-positive rate (31% of concussed) at the chosen threshold. So even when a single cutoff looks decision-efficient, the cross-layer adjudication rejects it in favour of longitudinal within-patient comparison plus a specific channel (vestibulo-ocular examination, a glial/neuronal biomarker panel), and marks any classification resting on the non-specific sum alone as a misleading, potentially LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE proxy for true injury status.

reasoning_traces.think: The second cluster turns from diagnosis to the physics of supply, demand, and catastrophic timing. The biomarker ratio (p4) shows that the latent injury type is resolved only by fusing mechanistically distinct channels — a glial blood-brain-barrier marker and a neuronal marker — whose ratio (GNR, focal ~1.77 versus diffuse ~0.48) and joint panel (ALERT-TBI sensitivity 97.6%, NPV 99.6%, specificity 36.4%) carry information neither channel carries alone, and whose high-NPV/low-specificity asymmetry dictates a rule-out rather than a rule-in use. The hypoxia invariant (p5) then establishes that functional outcome is governed by a local supply-duration threshold (brain tissue oxygen below ten mmHg for more than fifteen minutes) rather than by the headline pressure proxy: in the cooling pilot, oxygenation and six-month outcome improved even though ICP and CPP did not change, proving pressure is not the sole causal channel and that a local supply observable is indispensable. The flow-metabolism coupling invariant (p6) generalises this into a constraint on intervention: lowering demand is protective only if supply is lowered proportionally so the CBF/CMRO2 coupling and autoregulation are preserved; propofol lowers ICP yet its hypotension can lower CPP and break the match, so 'lower the pressure' is the wrong objective. Finally the Second Impact Syndrome threshold (p3) supplies the catastrophic-timing counterpart: re-loading inside an unrecovered refractory window can cause disproportionate, fatal failure from a mild second impact, a nonlinear tail risk that no linear load model captures. The retrocausal genealogy here is the field's repeated discovery that the proxy was hiding the true causal channel — ICP-guided therapy alone failed to prevent hypoxic-ischemic damage, single biomarkers failed in polytrauma, and animal neuroprotection failed in humans — each a scar teaching that the headline metric was not the mechanism. The theory-of-mind pressure is on the intensivist or coach who wants a single number to optimise (ICP, load, a clearance score) and thereby over-credits an intervention that moves the proxy while breaking the underlying coupling or ignoring the refractory window. The cross-layer veto adjudicates decisively: the physiology layer vetoes any high-EV call that optimises a proxy while breaking supply-demand coupling or re-loading inside the refractory window, because the local supply-duration threshold and the recovery-gated catastrophic threshold are the true determinants of outcome. Composing p3, p4, p5 and p6 yields the unified discipline: fuse mechanistically distinct, time-resolved channels; match the decision to the channel's NPV/specificity asymmetry; preserve the supply-demand coupling rather than a headline proxy; and enforce the recovery window against nonlinear tail risk. Where the calibration channel is absent, mark the latent state unidentifiable rather than laundering a proxy into action. The practical corollary for any simulator is that the reward must be scored on the true latent outcome (functional recovery, avoided catastrophic failure), not on the proxy that the agent can most easily move, otherwise the agent will learn to optimise the number while breaking the coupling or ignoring the window — exactly the failure mode the clinical literature documents.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The supply-demand and timing invariants carry the scar of repeatedly discovering that the headline proxy was hiding the true causal channel. ICP/CPP-guided treatment alone was shown not to prevent hypoxic-ischemic damage, while a local brain-oxygenation threshold (PbtiO2 < 10 mmHg for > 15 minutes) proved more important for functional outcome; single biomarkers failed in polytrauma because extracranial sources elevated them, forcing a complementary panel; and the cooling pilot improved oxygenation and outcome without changing pressure, exposing pressure as an incomplete proxy. Each finding descends from earlier over-confidence in a single number, and the modern protocol exists to stop that over-confidence by fusing distinct channels, preserving coupling, and enforcing the refractory window that Second Impact Syndrome reveals.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The belief clash under pressure is between the intensivist or coach who wants one number to optimise — ICP, a load metric, a clearance score — and the system's true multi-channel state. The clinician models the patient as 'pressure controlled, therefore safe', or the coach models the player as 'load reduced, therefore recovering', while the actual state may be locally hypoxic below a supply-duration threshold, or supply-demand decoupled by hypotension, or still inside an unrecovered refractory window. Correctly modelling the patient/player as a coupled supply-demand system with a recovery-gated catastrophic threshold prevents the premature comfort of a moved proxy and the over-credit of an intervention that breaks the underlying coupling.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Two vetoes adjudicate. The physiology layer vetoes any high-EV call that optimises a headline proxy while breaking supply-demand coupling: lowering ICP or load is rejected as protective unless the CBF/CMRO2 (or load-recovery) coupling and autoregulation are preserved, because propofol-style hypotension can lower CPP and worsen the state despite a lower proxy. The timing layer vetoes re-loading inside the unrecovered refractory window, because Second Impact Syndrome shows a mild second impact there can cause disproportionate fatal failure — a nonlinear tail risk a linear model misses. The unified veto is to fuse mechanistically distinct, time-resolved channels, match the decision to their NPV/specificity asymmetry, preserve coupling rather than a proxy, and enforce the recovery window; absent the calibration channel, mark the latent state unidentifiable.

universal_lens: A polymath audit lens for partially observable dynamical systems under intervention: never let a non-specific aggregate or a headline proxy stand in for a specific latent state; fuse mechanistically distinct, time-resolved channels and match the decision to their sensitivity/specificity/NPV asymmetry; preserve the supply-demand coupling rather than optimising a single number; and enforce recovery-gated refractory windows against nonlinear catastrophic tail risk. The unifying discipline is fail-closed calibration — when the specific calibration channel is absent, mark the state unidentifiable instead of laundering a proxy into action.
gsi_mapping: For GSI this compiles into clinical telemetry and bioenergetics of the injured brain: the neurometabolic cascade and excitotoxicity/neuroprotection balance, the PCSS specificity failure, the glial/neuronal biomarker panel (GFAP, UCH-L1, S-100β) with its timed kinetics and rule-out NPV, the brain-tissue oxygenation threshold (PbtiO2 < 10 mmHg > 15 min) that dominates functional outcome over ICP, and the CBF/CMRO2 flow-metabolism coupling that neuro-sedation must preserve. It also flags the corticosteroid mortality signal (CRASH) and the animal-to-human translation failure as cross-layer vetoes against mechanism-plausible but outcome-harmful interventions, and Second Impact Syndrome as a recovery-window constraint on rehabilitation dosing.
gse_mapping: For GSE the primitives compile into Coach-Mind simulation, deception detection, and DFS/portfolio tail-risk discipline: the PCSS false-positive invariant warns against clearing or sidelining players on a non-specific wellness sum; the biomarker panel is a fused structural-plus-functional classifier whose high-NPV/low-specificity asymmetry suits rule-out screening; the hypoxia and flow-metabolism invariants warn that a headline load or availability metric can look acceptable while local recovery supply starves or load-recovery coupling breaks; and Second Impact Syndrome is the canonical recovery-gated catastrophic tail risk that forbids stacking high-load exposures inside an unrecovered window. Compensation and timing, not proxy optimisation, govern the decision.
